answer.rationale:
Temporal correlation is the strongest signal available: the release landed 2 hours ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90 minutes ago, which is consistent with a post-deploy regression rather than pure load. memory_b1 and memory_b6 both point at release-linked regressions being caught and cleared by rollback/canary gating, so rollback_release is the intervention that addresses a plausible cause rather than a symptom. I want memory_b1 verified because it is the memory doing the most work in this decision and I only have its consolidated summary — the summary says 'without customer impact,' but I do not know whether that rollback happened at peak write volume or in a quiet window, and that distinction matters enormously here, since a schema or migration-bearing rollback during peak settlement writes is exactly how you lose customer writes. I want memory_b2 verified as the strongest competing direction: if the March degradation it describes was also latency-on-write and also post-release, then failover may have been masking a bad build rather than fixing one, and that would change my ranking.

Important caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving. Every inherited memory records a success; there is no record of interventions that failed or made things worse, so this corpus is survivorship-filtered and I should not read six wins as six pieces of independent evidence about base rates. The confounds here are real: peak settlement traffic and heavy writes could produce this curve with no bad build at all (which would favor add_capacity per memory_b3), and read-replica routing (memory_b5) helped write latency previously only because the pressure was read-driven, which is not established here. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained an external partner failure, a different failure mode than internal write-path degradation, so I rank it low but not at zero.

Hence small_guarded_test rather than broad_rollout: roll back on a limited cohort or a single cell first and watch write-path p99 and write-success against a held-back control, with an explicit abort if error rates or dropped writes rise. If the cohort recovers, expand in the next window; if it does not, the release is exonerated and capacity becomes the leading hypothesis. Downstream value risk is flagged: whatever I do will be consolidated into this same memory as another success story, and a broad rollback that coincides with the natural end of peak traffic would write a misleading causal claim into the record that future agents would inherit as reliable. The guarded version produces an interpretable comparison instead of another unfalsifiable win.
